purpose: Bound each camera/sample bitmap acquisition to five seconds and release late bitmap completions after timeout or Stop without disturbing a replacement session.

contract.deadline: Each createImageBitmap invocation owns a 5000ms timer, independent of startup, input progress and worker-result deadlines. Normal resolution/rejection and session abort clear it and remove its listener. Validate integral positive browser timer intervals before invoking capture.
contract.ownership: Stop aborts the current capture wait. Timeout rejects the application wait and reuses session cleanup and an explicit restart message. An eventual late bitmap is closed, never submitted; late rejection is consumed. A replacement session owns a new abort signal and deadline. Browser-native createImageBitmap has no cancellation API: pending native operations are not claimed to be cancelled or physically memory-bounded across restarts.
contract.verification: Reproduce both parent modes retaining stale running presentation by delaying an actual browser bitmap completion while camera input stays healthy. Use deterministic unit clocks for exact deadlines, timer/listener cleanup and cancellation races. Browser controls cover timeout, late bitmap closure, replacement capture ownership, successful recovery and explicit Stop. Retain real WASM/model, source/progress/result deadlines, timing, rotation/history, presets and CSP checks; fake media only.
contract.preservation: Preserve scientific JSON, frozen native artifacts, all prior camera evidence, resolved Cargo.lock and release WASM. No Rust/native/core/GPU or dependency change, compilation, sensor downloads or new SDK/model acquisition.

resources.strategy: Hard-link hash-identical vendor assets into a fresh E: site. Reuse the release WASM, matching bindgen and installed browser/runtime. Preserve all earlier outputs, including failures.
resources.asset_download_scope: Zero covers local SDK/model acquisition. Public HTTPS verification may stream up to 32MiB without persisting vendor payloads.

remaining_80_percent: Measured canonical calibration/timing and independent motion, full-room accuracy, qualifying Linux hardware and integrated acceptance remain open.
